standards.3.RL.1: Ask and answer questions, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for answers.
standards.3.RL.2: Recount stories including fables, folktales, and myths; determine the central message, lesson, or moral.
standards.3.RL.3: Describe characters' traits, motivations, and feelings, and how their actions contribute to events.
standards.3.RL.4: Determine word and phrase meaning, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.
standards.3.RL.5: Refer to chapters, scenes, and stanzas; describe how each part builds on earlier sections.
standards.3.RL.6: Distinguish the reader's own point of view from that of the narrator or the characters.
standards.3.RL.7: Explain how illustrations contribute to what the words convey: mood, character, and setting.
standards.3.RL.9: Compare and contrast themes, settings, and plots of stories by the same author about similar characters.
standards.3.RL.10: Read and comprehend literature at the high end of the grades 2-3 complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.3.RI.1: Ask and answer questions, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for answers.
standards.3.RI.2: Determine the main idea and recount the key details that support it.
standards.3.RI.3: Describe relationships among events, ideas, or steps using language of time, sequence, and cause and effect.
standards.3.RI.4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words in a grade 3 topic or subject area.
standards.3.RI.5: Use text features and search tools, including key words, sidebars, and hyperlinks, to locate information.
standards.3.RI.6: Distinguish the reader's own point of view from that of the author.
standards.3.RI.7: Use illustrations such as maps and photographs together with the words to demonstrate understanding.
standards.3.RI.8: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs.
standards.3.RI.9: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details in two texts on the same topic.
standards.3.RI.10: Read and comprehend informational text at the high end of the grades 2-3 complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.3.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words. Sub-points: (a) common prefixes and derivational suffixes; (b) words with common Latin suffixes; (c) multisyllable words; (d) grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
standards.3.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension. Sub-points: (a) purpose and understanding; (b) oral prose and poetry with accuracy, rate, and expression on successive readings; (c) context to confirm or self-correct, rereading as necessary.
standards.3.W.1: Write opinion pieces supporting a point of view with reasons. Sub-points: (a) introduce the topic and state an opinion in a structure that lists reasons; (b) supply reasons that support the opinion; (c) use linking words and phrases; (d) provide a concluding statement or section.
standards.3.W.2: Write informative or explanatory texts that examine a topic and convey ideas clearly. Sub-points: (a) introduce the topic and group related information; (b) develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details; (c) use linking words and phrases; (d) provide a concluding statement or section.
standards.3.W.3: Write narratives with effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences. Sub-points: (a) establish a situation and introduce a narrator or characters; (b) use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings; (c) use temporal words and phrases; (d) provide a sense of closure.
standards.3.W.4: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
standards.3.W.5: With guidance and support from peers and adults, plan, revise, and edit writing.
standards.3.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing, including some keyboarding.
standards.3.W.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.
standards.3.W.8: Recall information from experience or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes and sort evidence into provided categories.
standards.3.W.10: Write routinely over extended and shorter time frames for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
standards.3.SL.1: Engage effectively in collaborative discussions on grade 3 topics and texts. Sub-points: (a) come prepared; (b) follow agreed-upon rules; (c) ask questions and link comments to the remarks of others; (d) explain one's own ideas in light of the discussion.
standards.3.SL.2: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or presented in diverse media.
standards.3.SL.3: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
standards.3.SL.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant details.
standards.3.SL.5: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems; add visual displays when appropriate.
standards.3.SL.6: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation, to provide requested detail or clarification.
standards.3.L.1: Demonstrate command of standard English grammar and usage. Sub-points (a)-(i): functions of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs; regular and irregular plural nouns; abstract nouns; regular and irregular verbs; simple verb tenses; subject-verb and pronoun-antecedent agreement; comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs; coordinating and subordinating conjunctions; simple, compound, and complex sentences.
standards.3.L.2: Demonstrate command of capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Sub-points (a)-(g): capitalize words in titles; commas in addresses; commas and quotation marks in dialogue; possessives; conventional spelling of high-frequency words and of base words with suffixes added; spelling patterns and generalizations; consult reference materials to check spellings.
standards.3.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions. Sub-points: (a) choose words and phrases for effect; (b) recognize and observe differences between spoken and written standard English.
standards.3.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words. Sub-points: (a) sentence-level context; (b) meaning of a new word when a known affix is added; (c) a known root word as a clue; (d) glossaries and beginning dictionaries, print and digital.
standards.3.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances. Sub-points: (a) literal and nonliteral meanings in context; (b) real-life connections between words and their use; (c) shades of meaning among related words describing states of mind or degrees of certainty.
standards.3.L.6: Acquire and use grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships.

excluded_codes.3.RL.8: The official text reads '(Not applicable to literature).' No such standard exists.
excluded_codes.3.W.9: The official text reads '(Begins in grade 4).' Grade 3 has no W.9; Grade 4 has W.9a and W.9b.
excluded_codes.3.RF.1: Print Concepts ends after Grade 1. Not defined at Grade 3.
excluded_codes.3.RF.2: Phonological Awareness ends after Grade 1. Not defined at Grade 3.
